Allergies: Codeine
Transfer from OSH s/p tPA
NONE

History taking is extremely challenging as pt is very hard of
hearing and legally blind.

History below obtained mostly from
records.
The patient is a ___ yo.
WF w/PMH of CHF, legal blindness, IDDM,

HTN, who is very activey and high functioning at baseline, who
developed acute left-sided weakness earlier today.

She was in 
her
usual state of health until 7:35 this am, when her caregiver
noticed left-sided arm & leg weakness together with L facial
droop & dysarthria, together with confusion.

No recent falls,
injuries, fevers, chills or infectious symptoms.
EMS was called.

Upon their arrival, fingerstick glc was 100, vitals were normal,
and pt denied chest pain or shortness of breath.

En route, EMS
noted improvement in left hand strength and speech.

Code stroke protocol started at ___, a little over one
hour after the onset of symptoms.

BP 131/66, HR 73, Sat 100%, FG
was 104. ___ stroke scale on arrival was 10 (difficult to assess
___ legal blindness and hard of hearing).

Stat head CT at ___
showed no acute hemorrhage.
No acute changes on EKG.

Cr noted to
be increased, unclear if new or old (pt receives her care at
___).  ___ TeleNeurology recommended tPA.

Risks and benefits were discussed with pt and also with her
daugher and son-in-law (Dr. ___, an ER physician).

Received tPA 4.4mg bolus and started on drip with some
improvement of facial, arm, and leg weakness.

Exam on transfer
showed left facial droop, ___ strength in left extremities, and
some dysarthria.

No evidence of hemotpysis, hematemesis, or
intracranial hemorrhage after TPA.
She was then transferred to

On arrival here, pt initially mildly dysarthric per nursing, 
then
had acute worsening of dysarthria noted with confusion, stat CT
head obtained, was negative for hemorrhagic conversion.
Acetaminophen 1gm x 1 given for generalized pain.

ROS: complains of diffuse pain, and of dyspnea ("like I am
suffocating").
Per caregivers, pt had a CHF exacerbation in

___, and had been doing well but over the last week gained
approx. 10 lbs again.

Unable to obtain further ROS due to
communication difficulties.

CHF, HTN, IDDM, Renal insufficiency, Legal blindness, Hearing 
loss
PSH: unknown
Noncontributory
ADMISSION PHYSICAL EXAM:

General: sitting up at 45 degrees, moaning, slightly
uncomfortable due to dyspnea

- Head: NC/AT, no conjunctival pallor or icterus, no
oropharyngeal lesions
- Neck: Supple, no nuchal rigidity.

No lymphadenopathy or
thyromegaly.
- Cardiovascular: No carotid bruits; carotids with normal volume

& upstroke; jugular venous distention to above angle of jaw,
venous waveform normal with a > v; RRR, no M/R/G

- Respiratory: mildly labored and tachypneic, crackles at bases
anteriorly

- Abdomen: nondistended, normal bowel sounds, no
tenderness/rigidity/guarding
- Extremities: Warm, significant pitting edema at ankles

Neurologic Examination: very challenging due to communication
difficulties.

Mental Status:  Awake, alert, oriented to self, being at ___,
the date and year, and to it being ___ ___.

Does not 
know
why she is in the hospital.

Concentration maintained when
recalling days of week backwards.

Language fluent with mild
dysarthria and some stammering, and with intact repetition and
verbal comprehension; however, pt notably starts normal 
sentences
but ends up whispering or mouthing the end of the phrase, same
for longer words.
No paraphasic errors.

Follows two-step
commands, midline and appendicular.

High- and low-frequency
naming intact.

Registration ___ after about 3 attampts and 
recall
___ spontaneously, improving to ___ with category cueing.

No
ideomotor apraxia or obvious motor neglect, although full
assessment of neglect is difficult at this time.
Cranial Nerves: [II] PERRL 2->1 brisk.

VF full to finger motion,
including to DSS.

[III, IV, VI] Forced R gaze deviation, able to
cross midline only a little.

[V] V1-V3 with symmetrical 
sensation
to pinprick.
Pterygoids contract normally.

[VII] Mild left-sided
droop of lower face.

[VIII] Very hard of hearing but slightly
better on R. [IX, X] Palate elevation symmetric.

[XI] SCM
strength ___ bilaterally.
[XII] Tongue midline.

Motor: Some generalized wasting, especially of small muscles of
hands.
L pronator drift present.

effort and give-way weakness]

or DSS.

[Bic] [Tri] [___] [Quad] [Ankle]
Plantar response extensor on left, mute on right.

Coordination: No dysdiadochokinesia on RAM of right hand, no
ataxia dysproportionate to weakness on left.
Gait: deferred
DISCHARGE EXAMINATION:
Alert and oriented x 3.
Speech fluent.

L mild nasolabial fold 
flattening.

Intact

cells, and 
middle ear cavities are clear.

No facial or cranial soft tissue

Atherosclerotic calcification of the

IMPRESSION:  Interval resolution of a focus of hyperdensity in

No evidence of hemorrhagic 
transformation or any new acute intracranial process.

AP/LATERAL CXR (___): The heart remains stably enlarged with 
prominent tortuous aorta.

There are layering bilateral 
effusions, left much greater than right.

In the retrocardiac 
region, there is consolidation suggestive of compressive 
atelectasis.
The previously seen pulmonary edema has resolved.

Apical pleural thickening is now evident and given the patient's 
stated age is most likely chronic; comparison to more remote 
studies would be helpful to assess for stability.

Relative 
paucity of vessels in both apices suggests component of 
underlying emphysema.

arm and leg weakness and received tPA at OSH, transferred to
___ for post-tPA care.

# NEURO: Patient remained in the ICU for 24 hours of post-tPA 
monitoring.

On arrival to ___ ICU patient's exam was 
consistent with a partial right MCA or MCA superior division 
syndrome, with left hemibody weakness (arm>face or leg), right 
gaze deviation and and speech impersistence.

CTA was not 
performed given her impaired renal function, and patient could 
not tolerate MRI.

However, ___ showed a dense vessel sign in 
the M1 segment of the right MCA which subsequently resolved on 
repeat NCHCT on HD #2.

She had TTE which showed LVEF ___ with 
severe global hypokinesis of LV and moderate RV hypokinesis.

The 
hypothesized etiology of her stroke was cardioembolic secondary 
to low ejection fraction.

She was monitored on telemetry with no 
evidence of atrial fibrillation throughout hospitalization.

Her 
modifiable stroke risk factors were checked and showed LDL 58

For secondary stroke prophylaxis, patient's aspirin 
was increased from 81mg to 325mg daily.

Clinically patient's exam improved significantly during 
hospitalization.

On HD#2 in the ICU she had at least ___ 
proximal strength in her left arm and leg and her right gaze 
deviation had resolved.

On discharge her exam was improved with 
mild left nasolabial fold flattening, LUE and LLE at least ___.

# CARDIAC: Patient has known h/o CHF, and TTE on admission 
showed EF ___ with severe global hypokinesis.

On admission 
she appeared clinically volume overloaded with pitting edema,
4cm JVD and bibasilar crackles.

To allow autoregulation after 
her stroke her home Torsemide was held on HD #1 and she received
PRN IV Lasix boluses.
On HD #2 she was started on Lasix 40mg IV
BID (equivalent to ___ home dose of Torsemide 80mg BID).

Her 
home antihypertensives (amlodipine, isordil) were held and she 
received ___ dose of home carvedilol.

Home digoxin was continued 
and she received an additional dose for a low level of 0.7, 
which then improved to 1.2,.

- hydralazine 10mg qid, amlodipine 2.5mg qd
- carvedilol was decreased from 18.75 bid to 12.5 mg bid
